findings.declaration: ESS.LPS.lps_conv_div_free (reflected-kernel test function and its derivative)
findings.excerpt: have hpartial : ∀ (i : Fin 3) (y : Vec3), ψ.partialDeriv i y = -vlDeriv η i (x - y) := by
findings.problem: The proof builds the test function y ↦ η (x - y) as a `WeakTestFunction`, with smoothness from `contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id` and compact support from `Homeomorph.subLeft x`. It then proves its coordinate derivative is `-(∂ᵢη)(x - y)` by a chain-rule computation: `hasFDerivAt_id.const_sub`, `HasFDerivAt.comp`, `.fderiv`, `Function.comp_def`. `regularisedProfileConvolution_divergence_eq_zero` in RegularisedInitialData.lean repeats the same construction and derivative computation for a different kernel κ. Only the kernel name and the `fderiv ℝ κ (x - y) (basisVec i)` form of the result differ. The chain-rule block is the non-trivial part, and the two copies would have to be fixed in step.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a shared constructor and derivative lemma next to `testGradient` in CaffarelliKohnNirenberg/Leray/JSpace.lean. Both users already import that file, the target directly and RegularisedInitialData through JSpaceMollify.

  def WeakTestFunction.reflect (κ : Vec3 → ℝ) (hκ : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) κ) (hκc : HasCompactSupport κ) (x : Vec3) : WeakTestFunction (Set.univ : Set Vec3) := ⟨fun y => κ (x - y), hκ.comp (contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id), hκc.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.subLeft x), Set.subset_univ _⟩

  theorem WeakTestFunction.reflect_partialDeriv (κ hκ hκc x) (i : Fin 3) (y : Vec3) : (WeakTestFunction.reflect κ hκ hκc x).partialDeriv i y = -(fderiv ℝ κ (x - y)) (basisVec i)

The proof of the second lemma is the current lines 46–55, with κ in place of η.

In `lps_conv_div_free` the block becomes `let ψ := WeakTestFunction.reflect η hη.1 hη.2 x` and `hpartial i y := ψ.reflect_partialDeriv ..`. The `vlDeriv` form follows by `rfl` or `simp [vlDeriv]`. In RegularisedInitialData, `ψ` and `hψderiv` (lines 459–471) become the same two lines.
findings.benefit: The chain-rule computation is written and proved once, in the shared `WeakTestFunction` API. The two div-free proofs shrink to their real content: pairing with the weak divergence condition, then a change of variables. A change to the representation of `WeakTestFunction` would then be a one-place fix.

findings.excerpt:
have hcont : Continuous (fun x : Vec3 => ψ.partialDeriv j x) :=
          (hg.continuous_fderiv (by simp)).clm_apply continuous_const
findings.problem: `hint2` proves that `ψ.partialDeriv j` is continuous, compactly supported (via `HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply`) and hence in L². It then multiplies by an L² component to get integrability. This regularity argument for `WeakTestFunction.partialDeriv` is re-proved inline in many places, and no public lemma exists for it. Copies appear in JSpace.lean (`smoothSolenoidal_test_integral_zero`, the `hderivS` block, and the private `testGradient_hasCompactSupport`), in `regularisedProfileConvolution_divergence_eq_zero` (`hgradCont`, `hgradCompact`, `hgradLp`), and in `forcedHeat_divergence_pairing_eq_zero` (`hdc`, `hds`). The only partially reusable results are private or are stated for the whole gradient vector.
findings.proposed_change:
Add public lemmas in JSpace.lean for `ψ : WeakTestFunction (Set.univ : Set Vec3)` and `i : Fin 3`:

  theorem WeakTestFunction.continuous_partialDeriv : Continuous (fun x => ψ.partialDeriv i x)
  theorem WeakTestFunction.hasCompactSupport_partialDeriv : HasCompactSupport (fun x => ψ.partialDeriv i x)
  theorem WeakTestFunction.memLp_partialDeriv : MemLp (fun x => ψ.partialDeriv i x) 2 volume

The proofs are the current lines 105–110: `(ψ.contDiff.continuous_fderiv (by simp)).clm_apply continuous_const`, `ψ.hasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) _`, and `memLp_of_hasCompactSupport`.

In the target, `hint2` becomes `fun j => (memLp_pi_iff.1 hw.1 j).integrable_mul (ψ.memLp_partialDeriv j)`. Its under-hypothesis form is unchanged: `hw.1 : MemLp w 2 volume` and `ψ` is built from `g`, `hg`, `hgc`. The `hgradLp` block in RegularisedInitialData and the `hdc`/`hds` pair in LocalSolutionDivFreePairing reduce to one-liners. The private `testGradient_hasCompactSupport` can then use the new compact-support lemma.
findings.benefit: The same regularity argument appears in at least four files. After the change each user cites it by name instead of re-deriving it. The `hint2` block here drops from ten lines to one. Readers see the weak-divergence pairing argument without the regularity boilerplate.
